scope.context: Standard repository scan of the TLSe TLS/DTLS library, focused on pre-authentication memory-safety in network parsers.
limitations: Findings are source-confirmed but were not reproduced under ASan or a debugger.
The bundled libtomcrypt.c was reviewed for call-site safety rather than exhaustively audited.
x509.c is only compiled when TLS_FULL_X509 is defined and was reviewed for context, not as the default parser.
scope.runtimeStatus: Not executed; no C compiler or sanitizer toolchain was available in the scan environment.
scope.summary: Repository-wide review of all 16 files: tlse.c, tlse.h, libtomcrypt.c, x509.c, examples, build files, documentation, and test data.

assets: Process memory of the TLS/DTLS server or client
TLS/DTLS session keys and peer credentials
Availability of the service terminating TLS, DTLS, or WebRTC
assumptions: The embedding application exposes TLSe parsing to network input
The default build does not define TLS_FULL_X509, so the bundled ASN.1 parser is compiled
Validation is source-level; no runtime exploit was executed
attackerCapabilities: Send arbitrary TLS, DTLS, and STUN datagrams to a listening endpoint
Control record lengths, handshake fragment headers, STUN attribute lengths, and certificate DER contents
Act as the peer or as a malicious server/client before certificate verification
securityObjectives: Confine every network-derived length and offset to its allocated buffer
Reject malformed records, fragments, attributes, and certificates without memory corruption
Never perform length arithmetic or copies before validating attacker-controlled counts
threatModel.summary: TLSe is a single-file C TLS/DTLS 1.0-1.3 implementation with WebRTC, STUN, and SRTP helpers. Its attack surface is untrusted network bytes consumed by tls_consume_stream, tls_peerconnection_iterate, and the certificate ASN.1 parser. The primary boundary is the pre-authentication record/handshake parser: attacker-controlled lengths and offsets reach memory copies before peer authentication or certificate verification.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted network datagram and record bytes -> tls_consume_stream
Untrusted STUN datagrams -> tls_peerconnection_iterate and tls_stun_parse
Untrusted certificate DER -> tls_parse_certificate and the ASN.1 parser
Pre-authentication handshake state -> authenticated session state
